security_audit.summary: Most static external-command findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences and inline payload formatting. The skill still contains actionable SQL injection exploitation guidance, including credential extraction, authentication bypass, out-of-band exfiltration, and WAF evasion. No prompt injection text was found in the reviewed file.

remediation.issue: Actionable credential extraction and authentication bypass examples
remediation.suggestion: Reframe examples as defensive test cases, remove live exploit walkthroughs, and keep proof-of-concept evidence minimal.

remediation.issue: Out-of-band exfiltration payloads with attacker-controlled endpoints
remediation.suggestion: Replace exfiltration recipes with non-routable placeholders and focus on detection signals and safe validation.
Limit evasion content to authorized lab contexts or replace it with secure coding and validation guidance.

remediation.issue: Authorization guardrails are present but not enforced by the skill
remediation.suggestion: Add stronger upfront scope checks, stop conditions, and explicit refusal guidance for unauthorized targets.

content.value_statement: SQL injection testing needs clear scope and careful evidence handling. This skill helps authorized teams plan checks, understand techniques, and report fixes.
actual_capabilities: Identifies common SQL injection points in parameters, forms, cookies, and headers.
Explains boolean, error, time-based, UNION, and out-of-band SQLi techniques.
Provides payload references for common database engines.
Shows authentication bypass and data extraction proof-of-concept patterns.
Includes operational guardrails for authorized testing and data handling.
limitations: It does not verify authorization or enforce legal scope.
It can enable harmful activity if used on systems without permission.
It does not run tools or validate targets by itself.
Payloads may trigger monitoring, rate limits, or service instability.

use_cases.title: Plan an Authorized Assessment
use_cases.description: Create a scoped SQL injection test plan with target inputs, evidence limits, and stopping conditions.

use_cases.title: Understand Vulnerable Query Patterns
use_cases.description: Review how unsafe query construction can lead to data exposure or login bypass.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Security Report
use_cases.description: Organize findings, impact, proof-of-concept evidence, and remediation guidance for stakeholders.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Test Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: I have written authorization to test [application]. Create a scoped SQL injection test plan with inputs, evidence limits, and stop conditions.

prompt_templates.title: Triage One Parameter
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate analysis of a suspected issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this authorized finding for [parameter]. Explain likely SQL injection type, safe confirmation steps, and evidence needed for a report.

prompt_templates.title: Map Database-Specific Checks
prompt_templates.prompt: For an authorized assessment of [database type], outline relevant SQL injection checks, expected signals, and safe proof limits.

prompt_templates.title: Draft Remediation Guidance
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn these authorized SQL injection observations into a remediation report with impact, reproduction summary, and secure coding recommendations.

output_examples.input: Authorized review of a product search parameter with inconsistent responses.
output_examples.output: A finding summary covering tested input, response differences, likely injection class, impact, evidence limits, and recommended parameterized queries.

output_examples.input: Developer asks how to fix a vulnerable login query.
output_examples.output: A remediation note explaining parameterized statements, server-side validation, least-privilege database accounts, and regression tests.

output_examples.input: Security consultant needs an executive summary for a scoped SQLi assessment.
output_examples.output: A concise risk summary with affected areas, business impact, proof-of-concept boundaries, and prioritized remediation steps.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization, scope, and emergency contacts before using any payload.
Use the smallest possible proof-of-concept and avoid real user data.
Document requests, responses, and remediation steps in a secure report.
anti_patterns: Testing production systems without written approval.
Dumping full databases when a small sample proves impact.
Using evasion techniques to bypass controls outside the approved scope.

faq.question: Is this skill only for authorized testing?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is intended for systems where the tester has written permission and a defined scope.

faq.question: Does the skill run SQLMap or send requests?
faq.answer: No. It is documentation and workflow guidance. It does not execute tools by itself.

faq.question: Can developers use it for remediation?
faq.answer: Yes. Developers can use it to understand impact and plan parameterized queries, validation, and tests.

faq.question: Does it cover blind SQL injection?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes boolean-based and time-based blind testing concepts for authorized assessments.

faq.question: What evidence should a tester collect?
faq.answer: Collect minimal proof, request and response details, affected parameters, impact, and remediation advice.

faq.question: What are the main risks?
faq.answer: Misuse can expose data, bypass authentication, trigger monitoring, or disrupt services outside the approved scope.
